References / Textile / 129

BRATATAT T-shirt

A screen-printed T-shirt after Roy Lichtenstein: two firing gun barrels, red and yellow flames, a blue dot field, and the sound effect BRATATAT.

Source
V&A: BRATATAT, T.591-1997
Creator
Roy Lichtenstein (artist); Fruit of the Loom, Screen Stars label (manufacturer)
Made
Probably 1981
Style
Pop art (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Loud, graphic, playful
Evidence
Downloaded and inspected the V&A image of its copy, T.591-1997 (1400 × 2076 px), in a scratchpad. No image is stored.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The V&A describes a printed cotton T-shirt, probably made by Screen Stars (Fruit of the Loom) in the USA, probably in 1981, and probably made for a Lichtenstein exhibition that year. V&A.

The V&A says the design extends the final panel of Lichtenstein’s 1964 painting As I Opened Fire, which was based on 1962 comic panels by Jerry Grandenetti. The shirt omits the caption that crops the painting, and its dots differ from the painting. V&A.

Observed

  • A large oval of blue dots on white runs diagonally across the front of the shirt. The dots are coarse and widely spaced.
  • Two gun barrels in black and white point up and to the right; red and yellow flames with black outlines stream from them.
  • “BRATATAT” is printed in red capitals with a black outline and a jagged, uneven baseline across the chest.
  • A small patch of magenta dots shades the gun mounts at lower left.
  • The shirt is sleeveless (the sleeves appear to have been cut off) and is stained at right.

Why it belongs

The shirt shows how the style survives reproduction on cheap media: three flat inks, a coarse dot screen, and black line, which is also how it survives on screens.

The dot field is an oval with a soft edge made by the dots themselves, not a gradient.

Borrow

Give a dot field a shaped edge, such as an oval or a diagonal band, instead of filling the whole panel.

Set a sound-effect word at an angle along the direction of motion.
